note: KV-P6-V37 10-23: PV trunk structure options, kv_pv_pads_plan.py on the kv35 bind (BINDER2 bus_groups, = v3.6 PV lanes) with V/header/cmd(/flag) depths re-modelled by kv_pv_route.py; V-D-H shift fixed 0 (KV-P6-PV d218a2b98). member = pad per sink member (BINDER r8 landing, fanout counted 8x for V); entry = pads at the sink PARTITION ENTRY (one delay line per source-bit range per partition, --entry). Lane-flop and face numbers are hand-computed from the plan widths (128 b V per vport per partition, 1067 b vo per vport, 2 cycles per 1520-um partition hop, face budget 6 pins/um x 1900 um = 11.4k).

turnC.extra_lane_flops: ~+200k (up 1067 b x 2 cyc x (8-pk) hops per vport + 8-hop tapering down chain 128(p+1) b, minus v3.6 V lanes ~86k)
turnC.face_pins: pv_*_6|7 face ~13.7k, hub_C S/N face ~16.8k + cmd/rs > 11.4k budget -> G0 faces FAIL

mid.extra_lane_flops: pc rsp +~135k (KV-P6-PV estimate) + pv/vport re-cut; V-D-H = -2m by construction (ctl stays in hub_C) -> pads explode

ctlmid.extra_lane_flops: ctl<->hub narrow lanes ~4 hops (cmd 33 b, vport req 8x15 b, cfg, RH link); rs trunk/pe2 pads grow (RH and astk stay at hub end)

verdict: No re-route of V beats padding at the partition entry: required V depth = D + H + e (via-ctl distance) and the V bits are distinct per partition, so any physical detour costs >= the pad flops and adds face pins. Best pad-only = v3.6 lanes + entry-level pads 229k (V 155k, rs 59k). Below 150k needs the ctl moved (ctlmid 155k, V 30k but rs 85k / pe2 27k) or the rs trunk restructured too; turnC reaches 77k pads but costs ~+200k lane flops and fails face budget.
